note: Hancock County Conservation park, 93 acres, four miles northeast of Goodell, on a 21-acre lake for electric motors only. Swim beach, boat ramp, fishing pier and a 1.5-mile trail around the lake. The county lists sites 19-22 and 25-28 as having lake views. Generators are prohibited. Golf carts are prohibited. --Claude
summary: Confirmed $25 full-service, 45 sites (40 full-service 50/30/20A on 43-63 ft pads, 5 primitive), showers, dump, May 1 - Oct 15, online booking, 14-night maximum stay. Lakeview confirmed: the county's own pages give 8 sites with lake views. Possible lakefront upgrade on the pads nearest the lake (open lawn, ~25-50 m); reported, not changed. Pin fine.
flags: WATERFRONT (lakeview confirmed; possible upgrade): the county's site pages describe sites 19, 20, 21, 22 and 25 as having 'great lake views' and 26, 27 and 28 as having 'lake views' (8 of 40). The 21-acre lake is lake-sized. NAIP and Esri at 130 m show the west row of back-in pads off the campground spine about 45-50 m from the east shore of the lake's east arm, and the pads at the north end of the spine about 25-30 m from the shore. Both are across open mown lawn with scattered trees, no road and no driveway; a fishing pier sits on that shore. Under the open-apron rule that would be lakefront for perhaps 3-6 pads. But the county trail runs around the lake (likely along this shore), no source says any site is on the water, and I couldn't tie site numbers to pads. So I left it at lakeview; it needs AWH's call.

PRIMITIVE SITES: the park page counts 5 primitive sites, but they have no facility pages and no rate on mycountyparks. The stored note's '$10 primitive' could not be confirmed, so the fee base stays at $25.
Park page says the campground sits 'on the north west side of the lake'; imagery and Google both put it on the lake's southeast side, at the stored pin (~40 m from the pad centroid). Pin fine.
